name: gorse

attributes.attribute: hardy plant of Ireland and Britain

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Gorse is a hardy plant found across Ireland and Britain. It grows in harsh soil as well as in fertile land, and in spring its prickly stems break out in yellow flowers. People used gorse as a fast-burning fuel and as a hedge that cattle would not enter. In Wales, a sprig of gorse was thought to guard the wearer against magic.

okr.objective: Present gorse as the hardy plant used for fuel, hedges, and defense.
key_results: Gorse flourishes across Ireland and Britain.
Its stems bloom into yellow flowers in spring.
It burns as fuel and keeps cattle out of hedges.
Welsh custom used gorse against magic.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore, 2003
